paper_title: Shuttle Between the Instructions and the Parameters of Large Language   Models
caption: : The induction performance of SHIP and SFT on SNI with respect to the number of observed samples. The accuracy is the average accuracy over all seen and unseen tasks.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the induction performance of SHIP and vanilla SFT on the SNI dataset, with accuracy measured as the average over all seen and unseen tasks, plotted against the number of observed samples. The x-axis, labeled "observed samples," ranges from 1 to 6 on a linear scale, with integer tick marks at each unit. The y-axis, labeled "accuracy," ranges from 0.3 to 0.85 on a linear scale, with major gridlines at 0.1 intervals. The green line, representing SHIP, starts at an accuracy of approximately 0.81 when 1 sample is observed, remains relatively stable around 0.81 to 0.82 for 2 to 3 samples, dips slightly to about 0.79 at 4 samples, and then rises to approximately 0.83 at 6 samples. The blue line, representing vanilla SFT, begins at an accuracy of about 0.34 with 1 observed sample, increases to roughly 0.38 at 2 and 3 samples, then rises to about 0.40 at 4 samples, and continues to climb to approximately 0.45 at 6 samples. The legend in the bottom right corner identifies the green line as "SHIP" and the blue line as "vanilla SFT."
